articles.title: Magnesium is essential for health. But can supplements really help with digestion, muscle pain, anxiety and sleep? | Antiviral
articles.summary: Experts cite inconsistent evidence for supplementing with the essential mineral – and warn taking magnesium without a deficiency has risks. Danielle Shine says her Instagram inbox was filled with questions after Scarlett Johansson was quoted in the Daily Mail and other publications recently saying…
body: “I know that everybody is taking magnesium now. It’s so helpful,” the actor reportedly told beauty publication Byrdie.
Shine, a dietician, says celebrity endorsement of supplements is persuasive and always leads to an uptick in questions.
“The general sentiment was, ‘If she [Johansson] takes magnesium and says it works for her, then maybe I should be taking it too,’” Shine says.

Magnesium is an essential mineral that the body needs for blood pressure regulation, bone health and many other important functions. Because the body doesn’t produce it, diet is critical, with nuts, seeds, legumes, leafy greens and brown rice among good sources.

articles.title: Inside Seoul’s K-beauty ‘mecca’: I hunted for the best skincare at the world’s biggest Korean beauty store
articles.summary: What’s actually worth buying at Olive Young? A dispatch from the epicenter of Korean beauty, including the best skincare, face masks and hair care. Five of the best Korean skincare brands you can actually find in the US.
body: If flying all the way to Seoul into the eye of the storm for some face masks sounds like overkill, I have good news for the skincare lover reading this. More and more Americans are getting access to Korea’s largest health and beauty retailer, which opened its first US stor e in Pasadena earlier this year with a line that stretched a quarter-mile long. Last month, it made a buzzy debut in Sephora, where shoppers can buy 19 curated Korean brands in hundreds of locations nationwide. It’s been a relief for K-beauty fans in the US who have been stuck with the frustrating reality that the best stuff isn’t FDA-approved for sale here, or they can only find marked-up or counterfeit options on Amazon.

For the brick-and-mortar averse, I have more good news: Olive Young also opened online shipping for the US this year. Just as you would in its stores in Korea, you’ll find a dizzying array of brands on its site: familiar names such as Biodance and Abib, but also domestically popular ones that many Americans haven’t heard of yet, including Hanyul and Ilso.

articles.title: M&S links up with Sephora to lure younger shoppers
articles.summary: Beauty specialist will open branded areas in 100 Marks & Spencer stores and will sell its products on chain’s website. Business live – latest updates. Marks & Spencer has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract…
body: The French retailer is to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year.

Sephora relaunched in the UK in 2023 with huge fanfare and now has about 18 stand-alone British stores. The company is owned by LVMH, the luxury goods group led by Bernard Arnault, who with his family is among the world’s richest people with a $171bn (£129bn) fortune, according to Forbes.

The company has rapidly expanded on its second attempt to enter the UK market after closing a handful of stores in 2005, having failed make a dent in a competitive sector. The deal with M&S marks a new strategy in its expansion plans.

Analysts have said Sephora’s work with up-and-coming brands and collaborations with high-profile influencers on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube has helped the company reach its target female audience of 24- to 36-year-olds.

articles.title: Why are garlic presses so out of fashion? | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: It’s the gadget people love to hate – but maybe it does have a place in the kitchen? Why are garlic presses suddenly a no-no? Recipes now stipulate grating instead, but who wants lumps of garlic in their dinner?
body: Christina Soteriou, recipe writer at Ottolenghi Inc and author of Big Veg Energy, however, takes a more balanced approach: “A garlic press is not necessarily a no-no, and there can definitely be a time and a place for it,” she says. “It’s definitely quicker [than chopping], but I’d use it only when said garlic is going into a sauce, stew or braise.” Which is to say, in a dish where those lumps that concern Sally will cook down and dissolve almost entirely.

As with most things in life, Sally should just do her, though Soteriou does suggest sticking to one rule: “A garlic press for anything that’s going to be slow-cooked, and a Microplane, pestle and mortar, or minced for anything where it will be raw or cooked very quickly.” Just “never, ever buy ready-crushed garlic”, Chandler says. “That’s another business altogether and it tastes awful.”

articles.title: This Lakeside Town Was Just Named the Best 'Quietcation' in England
articles.summary: With hundreds of walking trails, peaceful lake views, and plenty of cozy tea rooms, Lake District's Windermere is the perfect place for a slowed down quietcation.
body: When I started traveling, I felt like I had to pack every day on holiday to the brim, but I often left feeling like I needed another to recover immediately afterwards. Now, unless I am traveling for work, I prefer a slower pace and days spent strolling around, people-watching, and really taking in the places I'm visiting—the traveler version of less is more, if you will.

The United Kingdom might not be the first place that comes to mind for island hopping or skiing, but it certainly is perfect for spending a few quiet days in nature. If your idea of a proper break involves switching off your phone, going for long walks, and generally doing as little as possible, a British quietcation might be exactly what you need.

The quietcation travel trend is all about escaping the noise and slowing things down, swapping packed itineraries and busy cities for nature, fresh air, and peaceful activities. No matter where you are, there are plenty of places across Britain where you can find the perfect setting for one.

articles.title: 24 Daytime Wedding Guest Dresses That Are Perfectly Appropriate
articles.summary: Wondering what to wear to an earlier wedding? A bridal stylist weighs in on the best daytime wedding guest dresses—from brands like Khaite, Staud, and more.
body: Most of us are accustomed to dressing for weddings that stretch well into the night. Move the celebration to daylight, however, and the usual evening formula—a floor-length gown, a little shimmer, a sleek black dress—reads as a total misstep. It’s a dilemma I know well from my years as a bridal stylist, and it usually prompts the same few questions: Is black still fair game? Is a mini appropriate? What, exactly, qualifies as daytime wedding guest attire?

The answer starts with the dress code. Take it at face value, then interpret it with a lighter hand—and a brighter palette—than you would after sunset. “Daytime formal,” for instance, still calls for long silhouettes, just without the heavy sequins of its evening counterpart. Where a structured black maxi can read decidedly somber at noon, a salmon-hued midi feels right at home at a midday cocktail fête. Ultimately, daylight demands you have fun with color, so don’t be afraid to embrace it.

articles.title: For Her Paris Fashion Week Debut, Fidan Novruzova Makes a Case for Vanity
articles.summary: Spring 2027 sees the Azerbaijani-Moldovan designer soften her signatures, play with color and proportion, and reframe vanity as a celebration of self.
body: Six years after launching her namesake label, Fidan Novruzova is thinking about vanity. Not, however, as one of the less attractive human impulses, but as something more gentle and liberating—the pleasure of looking, dressing, and indulging oneself. “There’s a way of thinking about your desires and your ego,” the Azerbaijani-Moldovan designer says from Paris the day before she makes her official Paris Fashion Week calendar debut, “in a way that it celebrates you.”

Her spring 2027 collection is fittingly titled La Vanité. But for a designer whose work has steadily accrued its own unmistakable codes—exaggerated square-toed boots, interesting collars, and rigorously sculpted outerwear—this season represents a moment of newfound confidence.

“I’m trusting that whatever I’m going to do is going to be me,” says Novruzova. Earlier in her career, she remembers questioning whether each experiment looked sufficiently “on brand.” Now, “I feel like I’ve been doing things that I would’ve not done five seasons ago, and I’m totally at peace doing and trying and loving something … or hating something that I’m doing.”

articles.title: Homemade Apple Butter
articles.summary: What to do with an overzealous orchard haul? Make apple butter.
body: Apple butter is basically applesauce that’s gone the distance: Cook apples until soft, purée them, then keep cooking to concentrate the mixture into a dark, velvety, intensely fruity spread. It’s that spreadable texture that gives apple butter its name—no actual butter involved. This version gets warm spice from cinnamon and cloves and a sweet-tart boost from apple cider.

For the best apple butter, use a mix of sweet and tart apples, such as Granny Smith, Fuji, McIntosh, Honeycrisp, or Golden Delicious. Unlike apples destined for pie, they don’t need to hold their shape—you want them to collapse. There’s no need to peel or core them either: The skins contribute flavor and the cores supply pectin, which helps the spread thicken. Once the fruit is soft, a food mill quickly separates the purée from the peels, seeds, and whole spices. Pressing the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer with a flexible spatula works too, but will require a bit more effort.
Spoon your homemade apple butter over waffles or ice cream, slather it on toast, serve it alongside pork chops, or layer it into Appalachian Apple Stack Cake.

articles.title: Adapalene 101: Everything You Need to Know About the Gentle Acne-Fighting Retinoid
articles.summary: Adapalene is the go-to acne treatment for everyone dealing with pesky breakouts. Here, experts break down everything you need to know about the hero ingredient.
body: Using Differin Gel for acne is a rite of passage for those of us who identify as having oily skin and deal with constant breakouts. Dermatologists love it. It’s in every acne-fighting guide. I love this gel so much that I slather it all over my face for supersmooth, clear skin. And its incredible results are thanks to this ingredient: adapalene.

If tretinoin is the gold standard of retinoids, then adapalene is its fun sibling that everyone loves. You get the same benefits without the harshness associated with tretinoin. Plus you don’t have to secure a doctor’s sign-off to get your hands on it. Access to adapalene is all yours with a simple click of “add to cart.” But why do experts love this ingredient so much?

“It is one of those ingredients where the science is much more interesting than the trend,” says Sonia Badreshia, MD, FAAD, board-certified dermatologist at Elite MD. “It has decades of dermatologic use behind it, and it works by normalizing cell turnover, so we are preventing clogged pores rather than simply chasing individual breakouts.”
